text:
anika: quick sync on rollout metadata model. trying to finalize semantics for pin signals + version affinities before we cut the next client release

josh: tl;dr: current `pin` semantics are inconsistent across SDKs. some treat pin as a placement request, others as a hint. causes silent evictions during canaries

peter: proposal: separate intent vs enforcement. add `pin.intent` (values: request|suggest|no_pin) and `pin.enforce` (bool). intent drives routing; enforce decides control-plane eviction guarantees

emma: i'm concerned about proliferation of booleans. can we instead use `pin.mode` enum: `preferred|strict|none`? simpler for SDKs to reason about
anika: `pin.mode` is nicer on the wire. mapping: preferred -> intent=request, enforce=false. strict -> intent=request, enforce=true. none -> intent=no_pin

josh: operationally we also need soft/hard TTLs for graceful rollouts. suggest `pin.ttl.soft_s` and `pin.ttl.hard_s` (seconds). example payload for older clients: `lease_s` will map to `pin.ttl.hard_s` during migration

peter: prefer explicit dot keys to avoid ambiguity in older languages: e.g., `pin.mode`, `pin.ttl.soft_s` etc. control plane still accepts nested JSON `{ \"pin\": { \"ttl\": { ... }}}` for human-readability

emma: add `rollout.rollback_signal` optional field (enum: automatic|manual|suspend). automatic triggers if quality metrics cross a threshold. needs to be plumbed into eval systems

anika: telemetry visibility: emit `pin_applied`, `pin_mode`, `pin_source` (client|control_plane|migration). include `applied_variant` and `candidate_variant` fields in traces

josh: migration plan: 1) SDKs log warning when `lease_s` used. 2) control plane accepts `lease_s` -> maps to `pin.ttl.hard_s` for 2 minor releases 3) expose a dry-run flag: `pin.dry_run=true` so we can test enforcement without actually changing placement

peter: about policy precedence: 1) explicit `pin.mode` in request 2) tenant-level defaults 3) global defaults. Make precedence deterministic and document order in the schema README

emma: edge case: `pin.mode=strict` but backend can't honor due to capacity. options: fail request, return `pin_status=denied` or fallback to `preferred`. prefer fallback+event for smoothness, but tenants can opt into `strict_enforce=true` at tenant-level to make stricter behavior

anika: agree. implement `pin_status` responses with reasons (e.g., denied_capacity, incompatible_variant, migratory_conflict). We should include HTTP header `X-Pin-Status` for quick inspection in logs

josh: testing: need a small soak where we set `pin.ttl.soft_s=10` and `pin.mode=preferred` for canary. watch for cache churn and client-side reconnection patterns. Also test `pin.dry_run` to ensure logging is correct

peter: schema-lint: add `rollout.hints` array of strings for compatibility flags (e.g., `prefers_kv_cache_v2`, `no_quant_cache`). control plane uses these to rank variants during selection

emma: doc note: encourage use of `rollout.hints` instead of embedding runtime flags in variant names. keeps variant taxonomy clean

schema-bot: created draft: https://github.internal/r/redwood/platform/schemas/pin-v2/diff?sha=rollout-metadata-v2 :white_check_mark:
anika: next steps: josh to open SDK deprecation PRs (lease_s warnings), peter to update control plane mapping + `pin_status` responses, emma to add rollback_signal integration with eval pipeline. quick check-in Friday 11am

peter: one last thought: consider `pin.lease_jitter_s` small jitter added to client refreshes to avoid thundering herd when many clients extend_on_hit. default 0 unless tenant opts in

josh: good call. we'll add `pin.refresh_jitter_pct` as optional float 0-100 in the SDK spec
anika: perfect. thanks everyone :raised_hands:
